title: Generative AI in textiles: Are physical samples obsolete?
content:
Traditional apparel sampling costs $1,800-$3,200 per style and can keep design-to-production cycles at 3 to 8 months.
BCG estimates virtual sampling can cut sample development costs by 60-70 per cent and reduce time-to-market by as much as 50 per cent.
Adidas has saved over one million material samples; Tommy Hilfiger reports an 80 per cent cut in physical sample production.

title: ICE cotton gains on weaker US dollar, persistent weather concerns
content:
ICE cotton futures extended gains to an 11-week high, supported by a weaker US dollar and persistent weather concerns across major producing regions despite profit booking.
Strong trading volumes, extreme heat in the US, India and China, and tightening production expectations reinforced the bullish outlook, while traders remained focused on August weather and the key 84-cent resistance level.

title: California’s $1 mn EPR rule targets $33.4 bn textile trade
content:
California’s textile EPR is moving beyond producer registration as marketplaces face seller-disclosure, producer-status and product-listing rules.
TexPro shows selected US apparel and household-textile imports reached $33.40 billion in January–May 2026, down 9.7 per cent YoY.
Vietnam became the largest source, while China and India drove most of the basket’s contraction.

title: Sri Lanka launches third ExpoScaleUp SME export cohort
content:
Sri Lanka's EDB, IFC and the EU have launched the third ExpoScaleUp cohort to strengthen SME export readiness and market access.
The four-day programme supports 25 high-potential SMEs in developing practical Export Marketing Plans with expert coaching.
Since January 2025, two cohorts have supported 50 SMEs; five secured first export orders and 38 gained certification or market exposure.

title: India’s Pearl Global reports highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q1 FY27
content:
Pearl Global Industries posted record Q1 FY27 results, with consolidated revenue rising 24.5 per cent year on year to ₹1,528 crore (~$160.6 million). 
EBITDA went up 44.1 per cent and PAT increased 51.4 per cent. 
Record garment shipments, expanding margins, capacity additions and diversified manufacturing across five countries supported growth despite geopolitical uncertainties.

title: Asia’s DPP divide will shape EU sourcing by 2029
content:
EU DPP rules are set to change apparel competition in Europe, requiring data on materials, substances and traceability.
Across Asia, Bangladesh builds capability, India links DPP to opportunity, Vietnam lags, and Turkey uses compliance infrastructure.
EU27 imports in January-April 2026 rose fastest from Vietnam at 15.8 per cent; China rose 8.6 per cent and Bangladesh fell 7.1 per cent.

title: How did Israel's Delta Galil achieve record revenue & profit in Q2?
content:
Delta Galil Industries has achieved record results in the second quarter of 2026, with revenue rising 7 per cent year on year to $570.6 million and net income increasing 13 per cent to $24.2 million.
Operating margin improved to 8.2 per cent, driven by strong performance in branded and private label segments.
The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue and profit guidance.

title: BGMEA, OCAB plan to attract Chinese investors to Bangladesh RMG sector
content:
Bangladesh trade body BGMEA and the Overseas Chinese Association in Bangladesh (OCAB) have launched an initiative to attract Chinese investment into the RMG sector. 
The initiative’s focus is on strengthening backward-linkage industries, reviving struggling factories and promoting joint ventures. 
OCAB feels more FDO is needed for modernising the upstream supply chain for Bangladesh's garment industry.
